title: Multi-dimensional latency signatures & heatmap dashboard per route/model/region
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide per-route / per-model / per-region p95 and p99 latency tracking with compact 'latency signature' representations and a heatmap-style dashboard that surfaces regressions and anomalies across dimensions (route, model, region, request_type). This ticket will deliver ingestion schema changes, aggregation pipeline, digest-based percentile computation, Grafana dashboards, and a synthetic load harness to validate sensitivity and false-positive rates.

Scope:
- Instrumentation: Add standard tags on all inference requests: route, model, region, zone, request_type, batch_size, input_token_count, kv_cache_hit. Ensure propagation through edge -> gateway -> runtime.
- Telemetry ingestion: Capture per-request latency (end-to-end and server-only) and token counts. Push to streaming pipeline (Kafka) with small proto payloads.
- Percentile computation: Use DDSketch for rolling p95/p99 in the hot path and maintain time-windowed TDigest snapshots for historical forensic queries. Store both sketches and compressed histograms in ClickHouse (or equivalent) for 1h/6h/24h rollups.
- Signature model: For each (route, model, region) maintain a compact signature: {median, p95, p99, qps, avg_tokens_per_request, 90th-token-rate}. Signatures will be hashed and compared to baseline to create a heatmap of deviation (delta p95/p99).
- Dashboarding: New Grafana dashboard with 3 coordinated panels: heatmap matrix (routes x models) colored by p99 regression magnitude per region; time-series detail for selected cell showing median/p95/p99 + token/s throughput; alerting matrix with live SLO breach count. Provide permalinkable slices and quick link to trace logs and request samples.
- Regression detection: Compute relative delta against rolling baseline (7d window) and absolute thresholds. Provide automatic anomaly tickets when: relative p99 increase >50% and absolute p99 > baseline+200ms for sustained 5 minutes, or p95 jump >100ms. Tune thresholds to reduce noise.
- Load harness: Extend synthetic harness to drive tokens/sec across route/model combinations with configurable seq lengths, batching, and caching flags. Report detection sensitivity and ROC for different sketch configs.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Instrumentation deployed to all runtime shards and validated in staging (sample rate 100% for test endpoints).
2) Streaming sketches are computed at 1m resolution and persisted; heatmap dashboard shows meaningful rows/columns and can filter by region.
3) Automated regression tickets are created in 80% of injected regression runs and false-positive rate <10% in baseline runs.
4) Documentation (Confluence) for tag schema, storage TTLs, and dashboard walkthrough completed.

Tradeoffs and notes:
- DDSketch provides relative-error guarantees which help compare percentiles across cardinalities, but it requires careful binning and memory tuning for long tails. TDigest is better for compression of historical snapshots; we'll store both for different use-cases.
- Storage vs. resolution: we will keep 1m sketch resolution for 30 days and aggregate to 15m/1h for 90/365 day retention to control costs.
- Compute cost: on-the-fly sketching in the hot path adds CPU; we'll run a canary with 20% sampling before enabling 100% for non-test traffic.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Schema design + initial proto + instrumentation PRs (edge/gateway/runtime).
- Week 2: Streaming consumer & sketching worker, ClickHouse schema, ingestion QA in staging.
- Week 3: Grafana dashboard and alert rules; synthetic harness improvements; create Confluence docs.
- Week 4: Canary rollout, tuning thresholds, handoff to SRE/Observability.

Related docs and links: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Latency+Signatures+Design, https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482, https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1991, https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/latency-signatures?orgId=1
